title: DC-area forecast: A few evening showers then a sizzling week
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Muggy with an isolated shower possible overnight and lows in the upper 60s to low 70s.

What's next? Heat and humidity build more tomorrow, peaking Tuesday through Thursday with highs at least in the mid-90s and heat indexes up to 100 to 105. Any storms should be isolated before a chance of scattered storms Thursday and Friday as a cold front closes in.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: A few showers linger this evening. Otherwise partly to mostly cloudy and muggy. Lows in the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow (Monday): Another muggy day with partly to mostly sunny skies and highs in the upper 80s to low 90s. Heat index values top out in the mid- to upper 90s. A stray shower or storm is possible late afternoon. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: A brief shower or storm remains possible again through mid-evening. Uncomfortable lows near 70 to mid-70s under partly cloudy skies. Confidence: Medium-High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather. Choose from free and paid ways to support us. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Partly sunny and very hot Tuesday through Thursday with highs at least in the mid-90s most spots, maybe some upper 90s to near 100. High humidity has heat index values reaching the upper 90s to around 105. Plan to stay hydrated and, if spending time outdoors, take frequent breaks in the shade. After the chance of an isolated late-day shower or storm Tuesday and Wednesday, there could be a better chance of scattered showers and storms Thursday. Confidence: Medium

The heat should start to ease a bit by Friday, with highs closer to 90 and perhaps a lingering shower and storm chance as a cold front passes by. That front likely brings Labor Day weekend highs down to the 80s. Confidence: Low-Medium

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Noticeably warmer and more humid, but not as harsh as the late-season sizzle on the way. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 30

Intense late-summer heat in 1953 pushed temperatures to 99 degrees, part of a prolonged stretch of 90-degree days and multiple record highs.
